signal: Aplos is expanding its nonprofit and church accounting platform with tiered plans and added budgeting, AP/AR, and donor-management capabilities

email.body1:
Jordan, saw Aplos broadening its platform across nonprofit and church accounting tiers.

A wider product range usually opens more in-market accounts than an SDR team can follow up on, and slow follow-up is where good replies die. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so your reps spend time in conversations, not research and CRM: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to Aplos's top three target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them?
email.body2:
Jordan, quick follow-up for Aplos.

Most SDR teams lose ground on response speed and follow-up volume, not list quality. The fix is rarely more reps, it's getting every account touched and re-touched fast enough to catch buyers while they're in market.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50-70 percent.
email.body3:
Jordan, last bit of proof for Aplos.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Aplos's reply rate likely compares to similar startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jordan, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If speeding up follow-up and ramp without adding SDRs isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Carrying a quota and a list is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your SDR motion? I'll tailor it to Aplos either way.
